result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but it lacks dedicated pedestrian signals. The environment is dominated by commercial land use with significant pavement wear and faded markings that reduce the overall safety and comfort for people walking.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven surfaces within the crosswalk area present a potential trip hazard.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: The signalized intersection does not appear to have dedicated walk/don't walk indicators for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light poles at the intersection

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian countdown signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection includes basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked continental crosswalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions result in significant exposure for pedestrians during crossings.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide roadway without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide turning radii
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians at the curb.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner curb near the red truck

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and traffic signals, but pedestrians must traverse a wide multi-lane roadway without a refuge island. The environment is primarily car-oriented with significant crossing exposure and wide turning radii.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without intermediate protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Refuge
hazards.description: There is no median or island for pedestrians to wait safely if they cannot complete the crossing in one signal cycle.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a car-oriented commercial intersection with basic but aging pedestrian infrastructure. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded and there is a lack of visible pedestrian-specific signaling.
